text:
Priority: urgent
Trace the owner's brief (the brief file at the repository root) to what is built (Sri, 2026-10-29: 'I feel like a lot of this is in my brief'). The brief's acceleration mandate (addendum 2026-10-13 'Athena owns acceleration'), its line 39 ('gets measurably faster, cheaper, and more correct'), A9 ('The numbers drive it') and A13 (learning curves per class) went two weeks with no mechanism, until a person asked why velocity was low. Nothing maps each brief requirement to a mechanism, an owner, a measure and its status. Build docs/brief-coverage.toml: one entry per requirement in the brief (each Part 1 bullet, each acceptance item and each dated addendum), with its mechanism (code path or role), owner role, measure and current status (met, partial, none), citing the brief line. Add a check run by the Hestia sweep that reads the map and the brief: a brief item with no entry, an entry with no mechanism, or a measure that is failing is queued once as a request through the shared steward request builder, citing the brief text, at priority high (urgent for anything about speed, per OP-23). Absorbs the requirements-engineer request 20261017-173506-k67x; close it citing this job.
Acceptance:
- docs/brief-coverage.toml has an entry for every requirement and addendum in the brief, and a test fails if a brief bullet or addendum heading has no entry.
- A test with a fixture brief and map shows the sweep queues one request for an unmapped requirement and one for a requirement whose measure fails, and none on a second run while they are open.
- The current map's gaps are listed in athena status.
- fmt, clippy with -D warnings and the test suite pass; CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
Files: docs/brief-coverage.toml, crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs, crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, CHANGELOG.md
